p3.original: On average, humans need about 2,500 calories a day to survive, depending on height, weight, and gender. The economist Brad DeLong estimates that the average worker in the early 1600s earned wages that could afford him 2,500 food calories. This worker lived in Western Europe. Two hundred years later, that same worker could afford 3,000 food calories. However, between 1800 and 1875, just a time span of just 75 years, economic growth was so rapid that western European workers could purchase 5,000 food calories a day. By 2012, a low skilled worker in an affluent Western European/North American country could afford to purchase 2.4 million food calories per day.
p3.zh: 人类平均每天需要约2500卡路里才能生存,这取决于身高,体重和性别.经济学家布拉德·德隆(Brad DeLong)估计,1600年代早期的平均工人挣得的工资可以支付他2500个食物卡路里. 这名工人生活在西欧. 两百年后,那个工人可以负担3000个食物卡路里. 然而,在1800年到1875年间,仅仅75年的时间里,经济增长如此之快,西欧工人每天可以购买5000个食品卡路里. 到2012年,一个富裕的西欧/北美国家中低技能工人每天可以购买240万卡路里的食物。

p4.original: What caused such a rapid rise in living standards between 1800 and 1875 and thereafter? Why is it that many countries, especially those in Western Europe, North America, and parts of East Asia, can feed their populations more than adequately, while others cannot? We will look at these and other questions as we examine long-run economic growth.
p4.zh: 是什么原因导致1800年至1875年间及其后生活水平迅速提高的? 为什么许多国家,特别是西欧、北美和东亚部分地区的国家,能够充分养活其人口,而其他国家却不能养活他们? 在我们审查长期经济增长时,我们将审视这些问题和其他问题。

p6.original: In this chapter, you will learn about:

p7.original: The Relatively Recent Arrival of Economic Growth
p7.zh: 经济增长的相对近期到来

p8.zh: 劳动生产率和经济增长

p11.original: Every country worries about economic growth. In the United States and other high-income countries, the question is whether economic growth continues to provide the same remarkable gains in our standard of living as it did during the twentieth century. Meanwhile, can middle-income countries like Brazil, Egypt, or Poland catch up to the higher-income countries, or must they remain in the second tier of per capita income? Of the world’s population of roughly 7.5 billion people, about 1.1 billion are scraping by on incomes that average less than $2 per day, not that different from the standard of living 2,000 years ago. Can the world’s poor be lifted from their fearful poverty? As the 1995 Nobel laureate in economics, Robert E. Lucas Jr., once noted: “The consequences for human welfare involved in questions like these are simply staggering: Once one starts to think about them, it is hard to think about anything else.”
p11.zh: 每个国家都担心经济增长。在美国和其他高收入国家,问题是经济增长是否继续提供与20世纪一样的显著的生活水平收益。 同时,像巴西、埃及或波兰这样的中等收入国家能否赶上高收入国家,或者它们是否仍应处于人均收入的第二层? 在世界上大约75亿人口中,约有11亿人的收入正在减少,平均每天不到2美元,与2000年前的生活水平没有多大差别。 世界穷人能否摆脱其可怕的贫困? 作为1995年诺贝尔经济学奖得主罗伯特·E. 小卢卡斯曾指出 : “ 这些问题对人类福祉的影响是惊人的:一旦人们开始思考这些问题,就很难考虑其他问题。 ”

p12.original: Dramatic improvements in a nation’s standard of living are possible. After the Korean War in the late 1950s, the Republic of Korea, often called South Korea, was one of the poorest economies in the world. Most South Koreans worked in peasant agriculture. According to the British economist Angus Maddison, who devoted life’s work to measuring GDP and population in the world economy, GDP per capita in 1990 international dollars was $854 per year. From the 1960s to the early twenty-first century, a time period well within the lifetime and memory of many adults, the South Korean economy grew rapidly. Over these four decades, GDP per capita increased by more than 6% per year. According to the World Bank, GDP for South Korea now exceeds $30,000 in nominal terms, placing it firmly among high-income countries like Italy, New Zealand, and Israel. Measured by total GDP in 2015, South Korea is the eleventh-largest economy in the world. For a nation of 50 million people, this transformation is extraordinary.
p12.zh: 一个国家的生活水平有可能有显著的改善。1950年代后期朝鲜战争后,韩国经常被称为韩国,是世界上最贫穷的经济体之一. 大多数韩国人从事农民农业. 据英国经济学家安格斯·马迪森(Angus Maddison)称,他毕生致力于衡量世界经济中的GDP和人口,1990年人均GDP为每年854美元. 从20世纪60年代到21世纪初,这段时期远在很多成年人的一生和记忆中,韩国经济迅速增长. 在这40年中,人均国内生产总值每年增长6%以上。 据世界银行统计,韩国的GDP现在按名义价值计算已超过30,000美元,这在意大利、新西兰和以色列等高收入国家中是稳固的。以2015年GDP总量衡量,韩国是世界第11大经济体. 对于一个拥有5 000万人口的民族来说,这种转变是非凡的。

p13.original: South Korea is a standout example, but it is not the only case of rapid and sustained economic growth. Other East Asian nations, like Thailand and Indonesia, have seen very rapid growth as well. China has grown enormously since it enacted market-oriented economic reforms around 1980. GDP per capita in high-income economies like the United States also has grown dramatically albeit over a longer time frame. Since the Civil War, the U.S. economy has transformed from a primarily rural and agricultural economy to an economy based on services, manufacturing, and technology.
p13.zh: 南朝鲜是一个突出的例子,但这不是迅速和持续经济增长的唯一例子。 其他东亚国家,如泰国和印度尼西亚,也出现了非常迅速的增长。 中国自1980年左右实行市场导向型经济改革以来,已经取得了巨大的发展. 美国等高收入经济体的人均国内生产总值也大幅增长,尽管时间较长。 自南北战争以来,美国经济从以农村和农业为主的经济转变为以服务业,制造业和技术为基础的经济.

p14.original: The Relatively Recent Arrival of Economic Growth
p14.zh: 经济增长的相对近期到来

p15.original: Let’s begin with a brief overview of spectacular economic growth patterns around the world in the last two centuries. We commonly refer to this as the period of modern economic growth. (Later in the chapter we will discuss lower economic growth rates and some key ingredients for economic progress.) Rapid and sustained economic growth is a relatively recent experience for the human race. Before the last two centuries, although rulers, nobles, and conquerors could afford some extravagances and although economies rose above the subsistence level, the average person’s standard of living had not changed much for centuries.
p15.zh: 让我们从简略地概述一下过去两个世纪全世界令人瞩目的经济增长模式。 我们通常将这称为现代经济增长的时期。(在本章之后,我们将讨论较低的经济增长率和经济进步的一些关键要素。 )快速和持续的经济增长是人类最近的经验。 在过去两个世纪之前,尽管统治者、贵族和征服者可以负担一些额外的开支,虽然经济超过了维持生计的水平,但几个世纪以来,平均人的生活水平并没有多大变化。

p16.original: Progressive, powerful economic and institutional changes started to have a significant effect in the late eighteenth and early nineteenth centuries. According to the Dutch economic historian Jan Luiten van Zanden, slavery-based societies, favorable demographics, global trading routes, and standardized trading institutions that spread with different empires set the stage for the Industrial Revolution to succeed. The Industrial Revolution refers to the widespread use of power-driven machinery and the economic and social changes that resulted in the first half of the 1800s. Ingenious machines—the steam engine, the power loom, and the steam locomotive—performed tasks that otherwise would have taken vast numbers of workers to do. The Industrial Revolution began in Great Britain, and soon spread to the United States, Germany, and other countries.
p16.zh: 在18世纪晚期和19世纪初,渐进、强大的经济和体制变革开始产生显著影响。 根据荷兰经济史学家扬·卢森·范赞登(Jan Luiten van Zanden)的说法,基于奴隶制的社会,有利的人口统计,全球贸易路线,以及随不同帝国而传播的标准化贸易机构,为工业革命的成功奠定了基础.工业革命是指1800年代上半叶,广泛使用电力驱动机械以及经济和社会变革.精巧的机器——蒸汽机、电机和蒸汽机车——完成了本来需要大量工人完成的任务。工业革命开始于大不列颠,很快蔓延到美国,德国等国.

p17.original: The jobs for ordinary people working with these machines were often dirty and dangerous by modern standards, but the alternative jobs of that time in peasant agriculture and small-village industry were often dirty and dangerous, too. The new jobs of the Industrial Revolution typically offered higher pay and a chance for social mobility. A self-reinforcing cycle began: New inventions and investments generated profits, the profits provided funds for more new investment and inventions, and the investments and inventions provided opportunities for further profits. Slowly, a group of national economies in Europe and North America emerged from centuries of sluggishness into a period of rapid modern growth. During the last two centuries, the average GDP growth rate per capita in the leading industrialized countries has been about 2% per year. What were times like before then? Read the following Clear It Up feature for the answer.
p17.zh: 使用这些机器工作的普通人的工作,按照现代标准往往肮脏和危险,但当时农民农业和小村庄工业的替代工作也常常肮脏和危险。工业革命的新工作通常提供较高的工资和社会流动性的机会。自我强化周期开始:新的发明和投资产生利润,利润为更多的新的投资和发明提供资金,投资和发明为进一步利润提供了机会。缓慢地,欧洲和北美的一批国家经济从几个世纪的迟缓发展到一个迅速的现代增长时期。 在过去两个世纪中,主要工业化国家的人均国内生产总值年平均增长率约为2%。那时候是什么样子的?读取以下 Clear It Up 特性以获取答案 。

p18.original: What were economic conditions like before 1870?

p19.original: Angus Maddison, a quantitative economic historian, led the most systematic inquiry into national incomes before 1870. Economists recently have refined and used his methods to compile GDP per capita estimates from year 1 C.E. to 1348.  is an important counterpoint to most of the narrative in this chapter. It shows that nations can decline as well as rise. A wide array of forces, such as epidemics, natural and weather-related disasters, the inability to govern large empires, and the remarkably slow pace of technological and institutional progress explain declines in income. Institutions are the traditions and laws by which people in a community agree to behave and govern themselves. Such institutions include marriage, religion, education, and laws of governance. Institutional progress is the development and codification of these institutions to reinforce social order, and thus, economic growth.
p19.zh: 安格斯·马迪森(Angus Maddison)是量化经济史学家,在1870年之前领导了对国民收入的最系统的调查.经济学家最近完善并使用他的方法汇编了从公元1年到1348年的人均GDP估计数,这是本章大多数叙述的重要对照点. 它表明,各国既可以衰落,也可以崛起。各种力量,如流行病、自然灾害和与天气有关的灾害、无力治理大帝国以及技术和体制进步明显缓慢,是造成收入下降的原因。制度是社区人民同意自己行为和治理的传统和法律。这些机构包括婚姻、宗教、教育和治理法。体制进步是这些机构的发展和编纂,以加强社会秩序,从而实现经济增长。

p20.original: One example of such an institution is the Magna Carta (Great Charter), which the English nobles forced King John to sign in 1215. The Magna Carta codified the principles of due process, whereby a free man could not be penalized unless his peers had made a lawful judgment against him. The United States in its own constitution later adopted this concept. This social order may have contributed to England’s GDP per capita in 1348, which was second to that of northern Italy.
p20.zh: 这样一个机构的一个例子是大宪章(英语:Magna Carta (Great Charter)),英国贵族于1215年强迫约翰国王签署. 《大宪章》编纂了正当程序原则,根据这些原则,自由人除非其同伴对他作出合法判决,否则不得受到惩罚。 美国在自己的宪法中后来采纳了这一概念. 这种社会秩序可能为1348年英格兰的人均GDP做出了贡献,后者的人均GDP位居意大利北部的第二位.

p21.original: In studying economic growth, a country’s institutional framework plays a critical role.  also shows relative global equality for almost 1,300 years. After this, we begin to see significant divergence in income (not in the table).
p21.zh: 在研究经济增长方面,一个国家的体制框架发挥着关键作用。 近1300年来,它也显示出相对的全球平等。 在此之后,我们开始看到收入的巨大差异(不是在表格中)。

p22.original: GDP Per Capita Estimates in Current International Dollars from AD 1 to 1348
p22.zh: 按现值国际元计算的人均国内总产值估计数(第1至1348年)

p95.original: Another fascinating and underreported fact is the high levels of income, compared to others at that time, attained by the Islamic Empire Abbasid Caliphate—which was founded in present-day Iraq in 730 C.E. At its height, the empire spanned large regions of the Middle East, North Africa, and Spain until its gradual decline over 200 years.
p95.zh: 另一个引人入胜和未充分报告的事实,是伊斯兰帝国阿巴斯德·哈里发在当时的收入水平很高,而后者是在730 C. E. 现今的伊拉克建立的。在其鼎盛时期,帝国横跨中东,北非,西班牙等大片地区,直到200年逐渐衰落.

p96.original: The Industrial Revolution led to increasing inequality among nations. Some economies took off, whereas others, like many of those in Africa or Asia, remained close to a subsistence standard of living. General calculations show that the 17 countries of the world with the most-developed economies had, on average, 2.4 times the GDP per capita of the world’s poorest economies in 1870. By 1960, the most developed economies had 4.2 times the GDP per capita of the poorest economies.
p96.zh: 工业革命导致国家间不平等加剧。 有些经济体起飞,而其他经济体,如非洲或亚洲的许多经济体,仍然接近维持生计标准。 一般计算表明,世界上经济最发达的17个国家在1870年平均人均国内生产总值是世界上最贫穷经济体的2.4倍。 到1960年,最发达经济体的人均国内生产总值是最贫穷经济体的4.2倍。

p97.original: However, by the middle of the twentieth century, some countries had shown that catching up was possible. Japan’s economic growth took off in the 1960s and 1970s, with a growth rate of real GDP per capita averaging 11% per year during those decades. Certain countries in Latin America experienced a boom in economic growth in the 1960s as well. In Brazil, for example, GDP per capita expanded by an average annual rate of 11.1% from 1968 to 1973. In the 1970s, some East Asian economies, including South Korea, Thailand, and Taiwan, saw rapid growth. In these countries, growth rates of 11% to 12% per year in GDP per capita were not uncommon. More recently, China, with its population of nearly 1.4 billion people, grew at a per capita rate 9% per year from 1984 into the 2000s and still average high rates of growth (more than 5% today). India, with a population of 1.4 billion, has shown promising signs of economic growth, with growth in GDP per capita of about 4% per year during the 1990s and climbing toward 7% to 8% per year in the 2000s and 2010s.
p97.zh: 然而,到20世纪中叶,一些国家已经表明,追赶是可能的。 日本的经济增长在20世纪60年代和70年代开始增长,这几十年中实际人均GDP增长率平均为11%。拉丁美洲的某些国家在1960年代也经历了经济增长的繁荣。 例如,巴西的人均国内生产总值从1968年到1973年年均增长率为11.1%。 在1970年代,包括韩国,泰国,台湾在内的一些东亚经济体出现快速增长. 在这些国家,人均国内生产总值的年增长率为11%至12%,这并非罕见。 最近,中国人口近14亿,从1984年到2000年代,人均年增长率为9%,平均增长率仍然很高(今天超过5%)。 印度人口为14亿,已显示出有希望的经济增长迹象,1990年代的人均GDP年增长率约为4%,2000和2010年代的年增长率达到7%至8%。

p98.original: Visit this website to read about the Asian Development Bank.
p98.zh: 访问此网站阅读有关亚洲开发银行的信息.

p99.original: These waves of catch-up economic growth have not reached all shores. In certain African countries like Niger, Tanzania, and Sudan, for example, GDP per capita at the start of the 2000s was still less than $300, not much higher than it was in the nineteenth century and for centuries before that. In the context of the overall situation of low-income people around the world, the good economic news from China (population: 1.4 billion) and India (population: 1.3 billion) is, nonetheless, astounding and heartening.
p99.zh: 这些赶超经济增长的浪潮并没有波及到所有海岸。 例如,在尼日尔、坦桑尼亚和苏丹等某些非洲国家,2000年代初的人均国内生产总值仍然不到300美元,比十九世纪和之前的几个世纪还低得多。在世界低收入者总体状况下,中国(人口:14亿)和印度(人口:13亿)的好消息仍然令人惊叹和振奋。

p100.original: Economic growth in the last two centuries has made a striking change in the human condition. Richard Easterlin, an economist at the University of Southern California, wrote in 2000:
p100.zh: 过去两个世纪的经济增长使人类状况发生了显著变化。南加州大学经济学家理查德·伊斯特林(Richard Easterlin)于2000年写道:

p101.original: By many measures, a revolution in the human condition is sweeping the world. Most people today are better fed, clothed, and housed than their predecessors two centuries ago. They are healthier, live longer, and are better educated. Women’s lives are less centered on reproduction and political democracy has gained a foothold. Although Western Europe and its offshoots have been the leaders of this advance, most of the less developed nations have joined in during the 20th century, with the newly emerging nations of sub-Saharan Africa the latest to participate. Although the picture is not one of universal progress, it is the greatest advance in the human condition of the world’s population ever achieved in such a brief span of time.
p101.zh: 通过许多措施,人类状况的革命正在席卷世界。 今天的大多数人比两个世纪前的前任有更好的食物、衣着和住房。 她们更健康、寿命更长、受教育程度更高。妇女的生活不太注重生殖,政治民主也获得了立足点。 虽然西欧及其分支一直是这一进步的领头人,但大多数欠发达国家是在20世纪加入的,其中新近出现的撒哈拉以南非洲国家是最新的参与国。 虽然情况并非普遍进步,但这是世界人口在如此短的时间内在人类状况方面取得的最大进步。

p102.original: Rule of Law and Economic Growth

p103.original: Economic growth depends on many factors. Key among those factors is adherence to the rule of law and protection of property rights and contractual rights by a country’s government so that markets can work effectively and efficiently. Laws must be clear, public, fair, enforced, and equally applicable to all members of society. Property rights, as you might recall from Environmental Protection and Negative Externalities are the rights of individuals and firms to own property and use it as they see fit. If you have $100, you have the right to use that money, whether you spend it, lend it, or keep it in a jar. It is your property. The definition of property includes physical property as well as the right to your training and experience, especially since your training is what determines your livelihood. Using this property includes the right to enter into contracts with other parties with your property. Individuals or firms must own the property to enter into a contract.
p103.zh: 经济增长取决于许多因素。这些因素中的关键是一国政府坚持法治,保护财产权和合同权利,以便市场能够有效和高效地运作。法律必须明确、公开、公平、执行,并平等适用于社会所有成员。 从环境保护和消极外部因素中可以回顾,财产权是个人和公司拥有财产和酌情使用财产的权利。 如果你有100美元,你有权使用那笔钱, 无论你花掉,借出,还是放在罐子里. 这是你的财产。财产的定义包括物质财产以及获得培训和经验的权利,特别是因为培训决定了你的生计。使用该财产,包括有权与其他当事人订立与您财产有关的合同。个人或公司必须拥有签订合同的财产。

p104.original: Contractual rights, then, are based on property rights and they allow individuals to enter into agreements with others regarding the use of their property providing recourse through the legal system in the event of noncompliance. One example is the employment agreement: a skilled surgeon operates on an ill person and expects payment. Failure to pay would constitute property theft by the patient. The theft is property the services that the surgeon provided. In a society with strong property rights and contractual rights, the terms of the patient–surgeon contract will be fulfilled, because the surgeon would have recourse through the court system to extract payment from that individual. Without a legal system that enforces contracts, people would not be likely to enter into contracts for current or future services because of the risk of non-payment. This would make it difficult to transact business and would slow economic growth.
p104.zh: 因此,合同权利以财产权为基础,允许个人与他人就使用其财产达成协议,在发生不遵守时通过法律制度提供追索权。就业协议就是一个例子:熟练的外科医生对病人进行手术,并期望得到报酬。 不付款将构成病人盗窃财产。盗窃是外科医生提供的服务的财产。在一个拥有强大财产权和契约权的社会里,病人-外科医生合同的条款将会得到履行,因为外科医生可以通过法院系统向该人索取报酬。 如果没有一个执行合同的法律制度,人们将不可能就目前或未来的服务订立合同,因为有可能不付款。这将使商业交易变得困难,并会减缓经济增长。

p105.original: The World Bank considers a country’s legal system effective if it upholds property rights and contractual rights. The World Bank has developed a ranking system for countries’ legal systems based on effective protection of property rights and rule-based governance using a scale from 1 to 6, with 1 being the lowest and 6 the highest rating. In 2020, the world average ranking was 2.9. The three countries with the lowest ranking of 1.0 were Somalia and Eritrea, with South Sudan at 1.5. Their GDP per capita was $875, $1,625, and $1,234.70 respectively. The World Bank also cites Afghanistan (GDP per capita $2,087.60) as having a low standard of living, weak government structure, and lack of adherence to the rule of law, which has stymied its economic growth. The landlocked Central African Republic (GDP per capita $979.60) has poor economic resources as well as political instability and is a source of children used in human trafficking. Zimbabwe (GDP per capita $2,895.40) has had declining and often negative growth for much of the period since 1998. Land redistribution and price controls have disrupted the economy, and corruption and violence have dominated the political process. Although global economic growth has increased, those countries lacking a clear system of property rights and an independent court system free from corruption have lagged far behind.
p105.zh: 世界银行认为,一个国家的法律制度如果维护财产权和合同权利,就具有效力。 世界银行为各国的法律制度制订了一个等级制度,以有效保护财产权和以规则为基础的治理为基础,采用1至6级的等级,其中1级为最低等级,6级为最高等级。2020年,世界平均排名为2.9.排名最低的3个国家是索马里和厄立特里亚,南苏丹为1.5。其人均GDP分别为875元,1,625元,1,234.70元. 世界银行还指出,阿富汗(人均国内生产总值2 087.60美元)生活水平低,政府结构薄弱,缺乏对法治的遵守,阻碍了阿富汗的经济增长。内陆的中非共和国(人均国内生产总值979.60美元)经济资源贫乏,政局不稳定,是儿童贩运人口的根源。 自1998年以来,津巴布韦(人均国内生产总值2,895.40美元)在大部分期间一直呈下降趋势,而且往往呈负增长。土地重新分配和价格控制扰乱了经济,腐败和暴力主导了政治进程。 虽然全球经济增长有所增长,但那些缺乏明确的财产权制度和没有腐败的独立法院制度的国家却远远落在后面。

p107.original: Since the early nineteenth century, there has been a spectacular process of long-run economic growth during which the world’s leading economies—mostly those in Western Europe and North America—expanded GDP per capita at an average rate of about 2% per year. In the last half-century, countries like Japan, South Korea, and China have shown the potential to catch up. The Industrial Revolution facilitated the extensive process of economic growth, that economists often refer to as modern economic growth. This increased worker productivity and trade, as well as the development of governance and market institutions.
p107.zh: 自19世纪初以来,出现了一个壮观的长期经济增长进程,在此期间,世界主要经济体——主要是西欧和北美国家——以每年约2%的平均速度扩大了人均GDP。 在过去半个世纪中,日本,韩国,中国等国家都显示出追赶的潜力.工业革命促进了广泛的经济增长进程,经济学家经常称之为现代经济增长。 这提高了工人的生产力和贸易,也促进了治理和市场体制的发展。

p109.original: Explain what the Industrial Revolution was and where it began.
p109.zh: 解释一下工业革命是什么,在哪里开始.

p110.original: The Industrial Revolution refers to the widespread use of power-driven machinery and the economic and social changes that resulted in the first half of the 1800s. Ingenious machines—the steam engine, the power loom, and the steam locomotive—performed tasks that would have taken vast numbers of workers to do. The Industrial Revolution began in Great Britain, and soon spread to the United States, Germany, and other countries.
p110.zh: 工业革命是指1800年代上半叶,广泛使用电力驱动机械以及经济和社会变革.精巧的机器——蒸汽机、电机和蒸汽机车——完成了本来需要大量工人完成的任务。工业革命开始于大不列颠,很快蔓延到美国,德国等国.

p111.original: Explain the difference between property rights and contractual rights. Why do they matter to economic growth?
p111.zh: 解释产权与合同权利之间的区别.它们对经济增长有什么关系?

p112.original: Property rights are the rights of individuals and firms to own property and use it as they see fit. Contractual rights are based on property rights and they allow individuals to enter into agreements with others regarding the use of their property providing recourse through the legal system in the event of noncompliance. Economic growth occurs when the standard of living increases in an economy, which occurs when output is increasing and incomes are rising. For this to happen, societies must create a legal environment that gives individuals the ability to use their property to their fullest and highest use, including the right to trade or sell that property. Without a legal system that enforces contracts, people would not be likely to enter into contracts for current or future services because of the risk of non-payment. This would make it difficult to transact business and would slow economic growth.
p112.zh: 财产权是个人和公司拥有财产和酌情使用财产的权利。合同权利以财产权为基础,允许个人与他人就使用其财产达成协议,在发生不遵守时通过法律制度提供追索权。经济增长是在一个经济体的生活水平提高时发生的,而当产出增加和收入增加时,生活水平提高。 为此,社会必须创造法律环境,使个人能够最充分地、最充分地利用其财产,包括买卖或出售该财产的权利。 如果没有一个执行合同的法律制度,人们将不可能就目前或未来的服务订立合同,因为有可能不付款。这将使商业交易变得困难,并会减缓经济增长。

p114.original: How did the Industrial Revolution increase the economic growth rate and income levels in the United States?
p114.zh: 工业革命如何提高美国的经济增长率和收入水平?.

p115.original: How much should a nation be concerned if its rate of economic growth is just 2% slower than other nations?
p115.zh: 如果一个国家的经济增长率仅比其他国家慢2%,那么它应该关心多少?

p130.zh: 劳动生产率和经济增长

p131.original: Sustained long-term economic growth comes from increases in worker productivity, which essentially means how well we do things. In other words, how efficient is your nation with its time and workers? Labor productivity is the value that each employed person creates per unit of their input. The easiest way to comprehend labor productivity is to imagine a Canadian worker who can make 10 loaves of bread in an hour versus a U.S. worker who in the same hour can make only two loaves of bread. In this fictional example, the Canadians are more productive. More productivity essentially means you can do more in the same amount of time. This in turn frees up resources for workers to use elsewhere.
p131.zh: 持续的长期经济增长来自工人生产力的提高,这实质上意味着我们的工作做得如何。换句话说,你们国家的时间和工人效率如何?劳动生产率是每个就业人员按单位投入创造的价值.理解劳动生产率最简单的方法就是想象一个加拿大工人在一小时内能做10块面包,而美国工人在同一小时只能做两块面包。 在这个虚构的例子中,加拿大人更富有生产力.生产力提高本质上意味着你可以在同样时间内做更多的事情. 这反过来又腾出资源供工人在其他地方使用。

p132.original: What determines how productive workers are? The answer is pretty intuitive. The first determinant of labor productivity is human capital. Human capital is the accumulated knowledge (from education and experience), skills, and expertise that the average worker in an economy possesses. Typically the higher the average level of education in an economy, the higher the accumulated human capital and the higher the labor productivity.
p132.zh: 是什么决定了工人的生产力?答案很直观劳动生产率的第一个决定因素是人力资本。人力资本是经济中一般工人积累的知识(从教育和经验),技能和专长。通常,经济的平均教育水平越高,积累的人力资本就越高,劳动生产率也就越高。

p133.original: The second factor that determines labor productivity is technological change. Technological change is a combination of invention—advances in knowledge—and innovation, which is putting those advances to use in a new product or service. For example, the transistor was invented in 1947. It allowed us to miniaturize the footprint of electronic devices and use less power than the tube technology that came before it. Innovations since then have produced smaller and better transistors that are ubiquitous in products as varied as smart-phones, computers, and escalators. Developing the transistor has allowed workers to be anywhere with smaller devices. People can use these devices to communicate with other workers, measure product quality or do any other task in less time, improving worker productivity.
p133.zh: 确定劳动生产率的第二个因素是技术变革。技术变革是知识革新与创新的结合,将这些进步用于新的产品或服务。 例如,晶体管是1947年发明的. 它使我们能够将电子设备的足迹小化,并使用比之前的管技术更少的动力. 此后的创新产生了更小、更好的晶体管,在智能手机、计算机和自动扶梯等各种产品中无处不在。发展晶体管使得工人可以在任何地方使用较小的装置. 人们可以使用这些装置与其他工人沟通,测量产品质量或者在更短的时间内完成任何其他任务,提高工人的生产力.

p134.original: The third factor that determines labor productivity is economies of scale. Recall that economies of scale are the cost advantages that industries obtain due to size. (Read more about economies of scale in Production, Cost and Industry Structure.) Consider again the case of the fictional Canadian worker who could produce 10 loaves of bread in an hour. If this difference in productivity was due only to economies of scale, it could be that the Canadian worker had access to a large industrial-size oven while the U.S. worker was using a standard residential size oven.
p134.zh: 确定劳动生产率的第三个因素是规模经济。 回顾规模经济是工业因规模而获得的成本优势。(更多读到生产、成本和工业结构中的规模经济。 )再次考虑一个小时内可以生产10片面包的虚构的加拿大工人的情况。 如果生产力的这种差别只是由于规模经济,那么,加拿大工人有可能在使用标准的住宅面积烤箱时,就能够使用一个大型工业规模的烤箱。

p135.original: Now that we have explored the determinants of worker productivity, let’s turn to how economists measure economic growth and productivity.
p135.zh: 现在,我们已经探索了工人生产力的决定因素,让我们来谈谈经济学家如何衡量经济增长和生产力。

p136.original: Sources of Economic Growth: The Aggregate Production Function
p136.zh: 经济增长来源:综合生产功能

p137.original: To analyze the sources of economic growth, it is useful to think about a production function, which is the technical relationship by which economic inputs like labor, machinery, and raw materials are turned into outputs like goods and services that consumers use. A microeconomic production function describes a firm's or perhaps an industry's inputs and outputs. In macroeconomics, we call the connection from inputs to outputs for the entire economy an aggregate production function.
p137.zh: 为了分析经济增长的来源,考虑一种生产功能是有用的,即将诸如劳动力、机械和原材料等经济投入转化为消费者使用的货物和服务等产出的技术关系。微观经济生产职能描述的是公司或也许是行业的投入和产出。 在宏观经济方面,我们把整个经济的投入与产出之间的联系称为总的生产功能。

p138.original: Components of the Aggregate Production Function
p138.zh: 总体生产职能的组成部分

p139.original: Economists construct different production functions depending on the focus of their studies.  presents two examples of aggregate production functions. In the first production function in  (a), the output is GDP. The inputs in this example are workforce, human capital, physical capital, and technology. We discuss these inputs further in the module, Components of Economic Growth.
p139.zh: 经济学家根据其研究重点构建不同的生产功能,提出了两个总体生产功能的例子. 在(a)项的第一个生产职能中,产出是国内生产总值。 这一例子中的投入是劳动力、人力资本、有形资本和技术。 我们在“经济增长的组成部分”这一单元中进一步讨论了这些投入。

p142.original: An economy’s rate of productivity growth is closely linked to the growth rate of its GDP per capita, although the two are not identical. For example, if the percentage of the population who holds jobs in an economy increases, GDP per capita will increase but the productivity of individual workers may not be affected. Over the long term, the only way that GDP per capita can grow continually is if the productivity of the average worker rises or if there are complementary increases in capital.
p142.zh: 一个经济体的生产力增长率与其人均国内生产总值的增长率密切相关,尽管两者并不相同。 例如,如果在经济中就业的人口百分比增加,人均国内生产总值将增加,但工人个人的生产力可能不会受到影响。 从长远来看,人均国内生产总值能够持续增长的唯一途径是平均工人的生产率提高,或者资本有互补性增长。

p143.original: A common measure of U.S. productivity per worker is dollar value per hour the worker contributes to the employer’s output. This measure excludes government workers, because their output is not sold in the market and so their productivity is hard to measure. It also excludes farming, which accounts for only a relatively small share of the U.S. economy.  shows an index of output per hour, with 2012 as the base year (when the index equals 100). The index equaled 110.5 in 2020. In 1977, the index equaled about 50, which shows that workers have more than doubled their productivity since then.
p143.zh: 衡量美国每名工人生产率的一个常见标准是工人为雇主产出贡献的每小时美元价值。 这一措施将政府工作人员排除在外,因为他们的产出不是在市场上出售的,因此很难衡量他们的生产力。也排除了农业,农业只占美国经济的相对较小份额. 农业显示的时速产出指数,以2012年为基年(当指数等于100).2020年的指数相当于110.5.1977年,该指数大约为50,这表明工人的生产力自那时起增加了一倍以上。

p144.original: Output per Hour Worked in the U.S. Economy, 1947–2020
p144.zh: 每小时输出一次在美国工作.经济,1947-2020年

p145.original: A graph has an X-axis with years progressing from 1955 to 2020 and a Y axis labeled Percent Change at Annual Rate. The graphed data moves up and down across a zero line indicating change year over year.  In 1970, 1974, 1981, 1983, 2008, and 2020, the rate was quite low, as the U.S. was undergoing recessions.
p145.zh: 一张图有一个X轴,从1955年到2020年的年数有进步,一个Y轴标注在年率的百分率变化.图表数据上下移动于零行间,表明年变化。1970年,1974年,1981年,1983年,2008年和2020年,由于美国正经历衰退,失业率相当低.

p146.original: According to the Department of Labor, U.S. productivity growth was fairly strong in the 1950s but then declined in the 1970s and 1980s before rising again in the second half of the 1990s and the first half of the 2000s. In fact, the rate of productivity measured by the change in output per hour worked averaged 2.8% per year from 1947 to 1973; dropped to 1.2% per year from 1973 to 1979; increased to 1.5% per year from 1979 to 1990; increased again to 2.2% from 1990 to 2000; increased even more to 2.7% from 2000 to 2007; and then decreased to 1.4% from 2007 to 2020  shows average annual rates of productivity growth averaged over time since 1947.
p146.zh: 根据劳工部的数据,美国生产力的增长在1950年代相当强劲,但在1970年代和1980年代有所下降,然后在1990年代后半期和2000年代前半期再次上升。 事实上,1947年至1973年,以每小时产出变化为衡量的生产率平均为2.8%;1973年至1979年降至每年1.2%;1979年至1990年增至每年1.5%;1990年至2000年再次增至2.2%;2000年至2007年增至2.7%;2007年至2020年又降至1.4%,这表明1947年以来的年平均生产率增长率为1.4%。

p149.original: In recent years a controversy has been brewing among economists about the resurgence of U.S. productivity in the second half of the 1990s. One school of thought argues that the United States had developed a “new economy” based on the extraordinary advances in communications and information technology of the 1990s. The most optimistic proponents argue that it would generate higher average productivity growth for decades to come. The pessimists, alternatively, argue that even five or ten years of stronger productivity growth does not prove that higher productivity will last for the long term. It is hard to infer anything about long-term productivity trends during the later part of the 2000s, because the steep 2008-2009 recession, with its sharp but not completely synchronized declines in output and employment, complicates any interpretation. While productivity growth was high in 2009 and 2010 (around 3%), it has slowed down over the last decade.
p149.zh: 近年来,经济学家们对美国生产力在1990年代后半期的复苏产生了争议。 一个学派认为,美国在1990年代通讯和信息技术的非凡进步的基础上发展了“新经济”。 最乐观的支持者认为,这将在今后几十年里产生更高的平均生产力增长。悲观主义者则认为,即使生产力增长更强劲的五年或十年也不能证明生产率的提高会长期持续.很难推断2000年代后期的长期生产力趋势,因为2008-2009年急剧但并非完全同步的衰退使任何解释复杂化,其产出和就业的下降急剧但并非完全同步。 虽然2009年和2010年的生产率增长很高(约3%),但在过去十年中却放缓了。

p150.original: Productivity growth is also closely linked to the average level of wages. Over time, the amount that firms are willing to pay workers will depend on the value of the output those workers produce. If a few employers tried to pay their workers less than what those workers produced, then those workers would receive offers of higher wages from other profit-seeking employers. If a few employers mistakenly paid their workers more than what those workers produced, those employers would soon end up with losses. In the long run, productivity per hour is the most important determinant of the average wage level in any economy. To learn how to compare economies in this regard, follow the steps in the following Work It Out feature.
p150.zh: 生产力增长也与平均工资水平密切相关。随着时间的推移,公司愿意向工人支付的工资数额将取决于这些工人产出的价值。 如果少数雇主试图向工人支付低于这些工人生产的工资,那么这些工人将得到其他寻求利润的雇主的更高工资。 如果少数雇主错误地向工人支付比这些工人生产的工资多的钱,这些雇主不久就会亏损。 从长远来看,每小时的生产率是决定任何经济体平均工资水平的最重要因素。 为了学习如何在这方面比较经济,遵循以下 " 工作结束 " 特征的步骤。

p222.original: Recall that compound interest is interest that is earned on past interest. It causes the total amount of financial savings to grow dramatically over time. p251.original: We can measure productivity, the value of what is produced per worker, or per hour worked, as the level of GDP per worker or GDP per hour. The United States experienced a productivity slowdown between 1973 and 1989. Since then, U.S. productivity has rebounded for the most part, but annual growth in productivity in the nonfarm business sector has been less than one percent each year between 2011 and 2016. It is not clear what productivity growth will be in the coming years. The rate of productivity growth is the primary determinant of an economy’s rate of long-term economic growth and higher wages. Over decades and generations, seemingly small differences of a few percentage points in the annual rate of economic growth make an enormous difference in GDP per capita. An aggregate production function specifies how certain inputs in the economy, like human capital, physical capital, and technology, lead to the output measured as GDP per capita.
p251.zh: 我们可以衡量生产率、每个工人生产的价值或每小时工作的价值,作为每个工人的国内生产总值或每小时国内生产总值的水平。1973年至1989年,美国生产力放缓。 此后,美国生产力大多回升,但2011年至2016年间,非农业商业部门的生产力年增长率不到1%.尚不清楚今后几年将实现何种生产力增长。生产力增长率是经济长期经济增长和工资增加的主要决定因素。几十年来和几代人之间,年经济增长率的几个百分点似乎差别不大,这在人均国内生产总值方面产生了巨大变化。总体生产职能规定,某些经济投入,如人力资本、有形资本和技术,如何导致按人均国内生产总值计量的产出。

p252.original: Compound interest and compound growth rates behave in the same way as productivity rates. Seemingly small changes in percentage points can have big impacts on income over time.
p252.zh: 复利和复利增长率与生产率相同。百分点的变动似乎很小,对收入会随着时间的推移产生很大影响。

p254.original: Are there other ways in which we can measure productivity besides the amount produced per hour of work?
p254.zh: 除了每小时生产的数量之外,我们还有其他方法衡量生产率吗?

p255.original: Yes. Since productivity is output per unit of input, we can measure productivity using GDP (output) per worker (input).
p255.zh: 对 由于生产率是单位投入的产出,我们可以使用人均国内生产总值(产出)来衡量生产率(投入)。

p256.original: Assume there are two countries: South Korea and the United States. South Korea grows at 4% and the United States grows at 1%. p271.original: Over decades and generations, seemingly small differences of a few percentage points in the annual rate of economic growth make an enormous difference in GDP per capita. In this module, we discuss some of the components of economic growth, including physical capital, human capital, and technology.
p271.zh: 几十年来和几代人之间,年经济增长率的几个百分点似乎差别不大,这在人均国内生产总值方面产生了巨大变化。 在这个单元中,我们讨论了经济增长的一些组成部分,包括有形资本、人力资本和技术。

p272.original: The category of physical capital includes the plant and equipment that firms use as well as things like roads (also called infrastructure). Again, greater physical capital implies more output. Physical capital can affect productivity in two ways: (1) an increase in the quantity of physical capital (for example, more computers of the same quality); and (2) an increase in the quality of physical capital (same number of computers but the computers are faster, and so on). Human capital refers to the skills and knowledge that make workers productive. Human capital and physical capital accumulation are similar: In both cases, investment now pays off in higher productivity in the future.
p272.zh: 实物资本类别包括公司使用的工厂和设备以及诸如道路(也称为基础设施)等物品。 同样,增加有形资本意味着增加产出。有形资本可以两种方式影响生产力:(1)增加有形资本的数量(例如,质量相同的计算机增多);和(2)提高有形资本的质量(同样数量的计算机但计算机更快,等等).人力资本是指使工人产生生产力的技能和知识。人力资本和有形资本积累类似:在这两种情况下,投资现在在未来的生产力提高中有所回报。

p273.original: The category of technology is the “joker in the deck.” Earlier we described it as the combination of invention and innovation. When most people think of new technology, the invention of new products like the laser, the smartphone, or some new wonder drug come to mind. In food production, developing more drought-resistant seeds is another example of technology. Technology, as economists use the term, however, includes still more. It includes new ways of organizing work, like the invention of the assembly line, new methods for ensuring better quality of output in factories, and innovative institutions that facilitate the process of converting inputs into output. In short, technology comprises all the advances that make the existing machines and other inputs produce more, and at higher quality, as well as altogether new products.
p273.zh: 技术的类别是“甲板上的笑柄 ” 。 早些时候,我们把它描述为发明和创新的结合。 当大多数人想到新技术时,发明激光,智能手机等新产品,或者一些新的神奇药物,便被想到. 在粮食生产方面,开发抗旱种子是技术的另一个例子。 然而,由于经济学家使用这一术语,技术仍然包括更多。 它包括组织工作的新方式,如编组线的发明,确保工厂产出质量更好的新方法,以及便利投入转化为产出过程的创新机构.简言之,技术包括所有使现有机器和其他投入生产更多、质量更高的进步,以及全新的产品。

p274.original: It may not make sense to compare the GDPs of China and say, Benin, simply because of the great difference in population size. To understand economic growth, which is really concerned with the growth in living standards of an average person, it is often useful to focus on GDP per capita. Using GDP per capita also makes it easier to compare countries with smaller numbers of people, like Belgium, Uruguay, or Zimbabwe, with countries that have larger populations, like the United States, the Russian Federation, or Nigeria.
p274.zh: 仅仅因为人口规模的巨大差异,比较中国的国内生产总值和说贝宁也许没有意义。 要了解经济增长,这真正关系到一个普通人生活水平的增长,注重人均国内生产总值往往是有益的。使用人均国内生产总值也便于比较人口较少的国家,如比利时、乌拉圭或津巴布韦,以及人口较多的国家,如美国、俄罗斯联邦或尼日利亚。

p275.original: To obtain a per capita production function, divide each input in (a) by the population. This creates a second aggregate production function where the output is GDP per capita (that is, GDP divided by population). The inputs are the average level of human capital per person, the average level of physical capital per person, and the level of technology per person—see (b). The result of having population in the denominator is mathematically appealing. Increases in population lower per capita income. However, increasing population is important for the average person only if the rate of income growth exceeds population growth. A more important reason for constructing a per capita production function is to understand the contribution of human and physical capital.
p275.zh: 为了获得人均生产功能,将每项投入分为(a)项。 这就产生了第二个总生产功能,即产出是人均国内生产总值(即国内生产总值除以人口)。投入是人均人力资本水平、人均实物资本水平以及人均技术水平——见(b)。分母中的人口数的结果在数学上是有吸引力的。人均收入较低的人口增长。 然而,只有在收入增长率超过人口增长率的情况下,人口的增长才对一般人很重要。建立人均生产功能的一个更重要的原因是了解人力和物质资本的贡献。

p277.original: When society increases the level of capital per person, we call the result capital deepening. The idea of capital deepening can apply both to additional human capital per worker and to additional physical capital per worker.
p277.zh: 当社会提高人均资本水平时,我们称成果资本是深化的.资本深化的构想既适用于每个工人增加的人力资本,也适用于每个工人增加的实物资本。

p278.original: Recall that one way to measure human capital is to look at the average levels of education in an economy.  illustrates the human capital deepening for U.S. workers by showing that the proportion of the U.S. population with a high school and a college degree is rising. As recently as 1970, for example, only about half of U.S. adults had at least a high school diploma. By the start of the twenty-first century, more than 80% of adults had graduated from high school. The idea of human capital deepening also applies to the years of experience that workers have, but the average experience level of U.S. workers has not changed much in recent decades. Thus, the key dimension for deepening human capital in the U.S. economy focuses more on additional education and training than on a higher average level of work experience.
p278.zh: 回顾衡量人力资本的方法之一是审视经济中的平均教育水平。 表明美国拥有高中和大学学位的人口比例正在上升,这说明美国工人的人力资本正在深化。 例如,最近到1970年,只有大约一半的美国成年人至少拥有高中文凭.到了21世纪初,超过80%的成年人从高中毕业.人力资本深化的理念也适用于工人拥有的多年经验,但近几十年来美国工人的平均经验水平并没有多大变化. 因此,深化美国经济人力资本的关键方面更多地侧重于额外的教育和培训,而不是提高平均工作经验水平。

p279.original: Human Capital Deepening in the U.S.

p280.original: shows physical capital deepening in the U.S. economy. The average U.S. worker in the late 2000s was working with physical capital worth almost three times as much as that of the average worker of the early 1950s.
p280.zh: 美国经济的有形资本正在深化。2000年代后期,美国工人平均使用实物资本,其价值几乎是1950年代前期工人平均价值的三倍。

p281.original: Physical Capital per Worker in the United States
p281.zh: 美国每个工人的有形资本

p282.original: Not only does the current U.S. economy have better-educated workers with more and improved physical capital than it did several decades ago, but these workers have access to more advanced technologies. Growth in technology is impossible to measure with a simple line on a graph, but evidence that we live in an age of technological marvels is all around us—discoveries in genetics and in the structure of particles, the wireless internet, and other inventions almost too numerous to count. The U.S. Patent and Trademark Office typically has issued more than 150,000 patents annually in recent years.
p282.zh: 美国目前的经济不仅拥有比几十年前更受过良好教育的工人,拥有更多,更好的有形资本,而且这些工人能够获得更先进的技术.科技增长不可能用简单的图表来衡量, 但是我们生活在一个技术奇迹时代的证据却在我们周围—— 发现基因学和粒子结构、无线互联网和其他发明几乎太多, 美国. 近年来,专利和商标局通常每年发放专利超过15万件。

p283.original: This recipe for economic growth—investing in labor productivity, with investments in human capital and technology, as well as increasing physical capital—also applies to other economies. South Korea, for example, already achieved universal enrollment in primary school (the equivalent of kindergarten through sixth grade in the United States) by 1965, when Korea’s GDP per capita was still near its rock bottom low. By the late 1980s, Korea had achieved almost universal secondary school education (the equivalent of a high school education in the United States). With regard to physical capital, Korea’s rates of investment had been about 15% of GDP at the start of the 1960s, but doubled to 30–35% of GDP by the late 1960s and early 1970s. With regard to technology, South Korean students went to universities and colleges around the world to obtain scientific and technical training, and South Korean firms reached out to study and form partnerships with firms that could offer them technological insights. These factors combined to foster South Korea’s high rate of economic growth.
p283.zh: 这种经济增长的良方——投资于劳动生产率,投资于人力资本和技术,以及增加有形资本——也适用于其他经济体。 例如,韩国到1965年已经实现了小学(相当于美国幼儿园到六年级)的普及入学率,当时韩国的人均GDP仍然接近其最低点。 到1980年代末,韩国几乎实现了普及中学教育(相当于美国的高中教育). 在实物资本方面,韩国的投资率在1960年代初期约为GDP的15%,但在1960年代末和1970年代初期则翻了一番,达到GDP的30-35%. 在技术方面,韩国学生前往世界各地的大学和学院接受科技培训,韩国公司伸出援手,与能够提供技术见解的公司研究并建立伙伴关系.这些因素加在一起促进了韩国的高经济增长率。

p285.original: Since the late 1950s, economists have conducted growth accounting studies to determine the extent to which physical and human capital deepening and technology have contributed to growth. The usual approach uses an aggregate production function to estimate how much of per capita economic growth can be attributed to growth in physical capital and human capital. We can measure these two inputs at least roughly. The part of growth that is unexplained by measured inputs, called the residual, is then attributed to growth in technology. The exact numerical estimates differ from study to study and from country to country, depending on how researchers measured these three main factors and over what time horizons. For studies of the U.S. economy, three lessons commonly emerge from growth accounting studies.
p285.zh: 自1950年代后期以来,经济学家们进行了增长会计研究,以确定有形和人力资本的深化和技术对增长的贡献程度.通常的方法是利用总生产功能来估计人均经济增长的多少可归因于有形资本和人力资本的增长。 我们至少可以粗略地衡量这两个投入。增长中被计量投入所解释的部分,称为剩余部分,然后归结于技术增长。准确的数字估计因研究而异,因国家而异,这取决于研究人员如何衡量这三个主要因素和在何种时间范围内。 对于对美国经济的研究,增长会计研究中通常会得出三个教训.

p286.original: First, technology is typically the most important contributor to U.S. economic growth. Growth in human capital and physical capital often explains only half or less than half of the economic growth that occurs. New ways of doing things are tremendously important.
p286.zh: 首先,技术通常是美国经济增长的最重要贡献者。人力资本和有形资本的增长往往只能解释所实现的经济增长的一半或不到一半的原因。新的办事方式极为重要。

p287.original: Second, while investment in physical capital is essential to growth in labor productivity and GDP per capita, building human capital is at least as important. Economic growth is not just a matter of more machines and buildings. One vivid example of the power of human capital and technological knowledge occurred in Europe in the years after World War II (1939–1945). During the war, a large share of Europe’s physical capital, such as factories, roads, and vehicles, was destroyed. Europe also lost an overwhelming amount of human capital in the form of millions of men, women, and children who died during the war. However, the powerful combination of skilled workers and technological knowledge, working within a market-oriented economic framework, rebuilt Europe’s productive capacity to an even higher level within less than two decades.
p287.zh: 第二,虽然对有形资本的投资对提高劳动生产率和人均国内生产总值至关重要,但建设人力资本至少同样重要。经济增长不仅仅是更多机器和建筑物的问题。 二战结束后(1939–1945年),欧洲出现了人力资本和技术知识力量的生动例子.战争期间,工厂,道路,车辆等欧洲有形资本的很大一部分被摧毁. 欧洲还损失了大量的人力资本,包括数百万在战争中死亡的男女老幼。 然而,技术工人和技术知识的强大结合,在面向市场的经济框架内工作,在不到20年的时间里使欧洲的生产能力重建到更高水平。

p288.original: A third lesson is that these three factors of human capital, physical capital, and technology work together. Workers with a higher level of education and skills are often better at coming up with new technological innovations. These technological innovations are often ideas that cannot increase production until they become a part of new investment in physical capital. New machines that embody technological innovations often require additional training, which builds worker skills further. If the recipe for economic growth is to succeed, an economy needs all the ingredients of the aggregate production function. See the following Clear It Up feature for an example of how human capital, physical capital, and technology can combine to significantly impact lives.
p288.zh: 第三个教训是,人力资本、有形资本和技术这三个因素共同发挥作用。受过更高水平教育和技能的工人往往更适合进行新的技术革新。 这些技术创新往往是一些想法,在成为对有形资本的新投资的一部分之前无法增加生产。体现技术创新的新机器往往需要更多的培训,这可以进一步培养工人的技能。 如果经济增长的良方要取得成功,经济就需要总生产功能的所有成分。 以下的Clear It Up 特征以说明人力资本、有形资本和技术如何能够结合对生活产生重大影响。

p289.original: How do girls’ education and economic growth relate in low-income countries?
p289.zh: 低收入国家的女童教育和经济增长有何关系?

p290.original: In the early 2000s, according to the World Bank, about 110 million children between the ages of 6 and 11 were not in school—and about two-thirds of them were girls. In Afghanistan, for example, the literacy rate for those aged 15-24 for the period 2005-2014 was 62% for males and only 32% for females.  In Benin, in West Africa, it was 55% for males and 31% for females.  In Nigeria, Africa’s most populous country, it was 76% for males and 58 percent for females.
p290.zh: 根据世界银行的统计,2000年代初期,约有1.1亿6至11岁的儿童没有上学,其中约三分之二是女孩。 例如,在阿富汗,2005-2014年期间,15至24岁人口的识字率为男性62%,女性仅为32%。 在贝宁、西非,男性为55%,女性为31%。 非洲人口最多的国家尼日利亚的男性为76%,女性为58%。

p291.original: Whenever any child does not receive a basic education, it is both a human and an economic loss. In low-income countries, wages typically increase by an average of 10 to 20% with each additional year of education. There is, however, some intriguing evidence that helping girls in low-income countries to close the education gap with boys may be especially important, because of the social role that many of the girls will play as mothers and homemakers.
p291.zh: 只要任何儿童没有接受基础教育,就既是一种人的损失,也是一种经济损失。 在低收入国家,工资通常随着每增加一年的教育而平均增加10%至20%。 然而,一些令人感兴趣的证据表明,帮助低收入国家的女孩缩小与男孩的教育差距可能特别重要,因为许多女孩将作为母亲和家庭主妇发挥社会作用。

p292.original: Girls in low-income countries who receive more education tend to grow up to have fewer, healthier, better-educated children. Their children are more likely to be better nourished and to receive basic health care like immunizations. Economic research on women in low-income economies backs up these findings. When 20 women obtain one additional year of schooling, as a group they will, on average, have one less child. When 1,000 women obtain one additional year of schooling, on average one to two fewer women from that group will die in childbirth. When a woman stays in school an additional year, that factor alone means that, on average, each of her children will spend an additional half-year in school. Education for girls is a good investment because it is an investment in economic growth with benefits beyond the current generation.
p292.zh: 在低收入国家,受教育程度较高的女孩往往成长为较少、更健康、更受过良好教育的儿童。 他们的孩子更有可能得到更好的营养,并获得基本保健,如免疫接种。有关低收入经济体妇女的经济研究支持了这些调查结果。20名妇女如果再获得一年的教育,作为一个群体,她们平均会少生一个孩子。 如果有1 000名妇女再获得一年的教育,该群体中平均有1至2名妇女死于分娩。 如果一名妇女再留学一年,仅这一因素本身就意味着,平均而言,她每个子女将多花半年时间上学。女童教育是一项良好的投资,因为它是对经济增长的投资,其利益超越了当代人。

p293.original: A Healthy Climate for Economic Growth
p293.zh: 促进经济增长的健康气候

p294.original: While physical and human capital deepening and better technology are important, equally important to a nation’s well-being is the climate or system within which these inputs are cultivated. Both the type of market economy and a legal system that governs and sustains property rights and contractual rights are important contributors to a healthy economic climate.
p294.zh: 虽然物质和人力资本的深化和更好的技术是重要的,但是对于一个国家的福祉来说,同样重要的是培育这些投入的气候或制度。市场经济类型和管辖和维持产权和合同权利的法律制度都是健康经济环境的重要促进因素。

p295.original: A healthy economic climate usually involves some sort of market orientation at the microeconomic, individual, or firm decision-making level. Markets that allow personal and business rewards and incentives for increasing human and physical capital encourage overall macroeconomic growth. For example, when workers participate in a competitive and well-functioning labor market, they have an incentive to acquire additional human capital, because additional education and skills will pay off in higher wages. Firms have an incentive to invest in physical capital and in training workers, because they expect to earn higher profits for their shareholders. Both individuals and firms look for new technologies, because even small inventions can make work easier or lead to product improvement. Collectively, such individual and business decisions made within a market structure add up to macroeconomic growth. Much of the rapid growth since the late nineteenth century has come from harnessing the power of competitive markets to allocate resources. This market orientation typically reaches beyond national borders and includes openness to international trade.
p295.zh: 健康的经济环境通常涉及微观经济、个人或公司决策一级的某种市场导向。允许个人和企业奖励和鼓励增加人力和物质资本的市场鼓励宏观经济的全面增长。 例如,当工人参与竞争性的、运作良好的劳动力市场时,他们就会有获得额外人力资本的动力,因为额外的教育和技能将以更高的工资得到回报。公司有动力投资于有形资本和培训工人,因为它们期望为股东赚取更高的利润。个人和公司都寻找新技术,因为即使是小的发明也能使工作更加容易或导致产品的改进.集体而言,在市场结构内作出的这种个人和商业决定,增加了宏观经济的增长。 自十九世纪末以来,快速增长的大部分来自利用竞争性市场的力量来分配资源。 这种市场导向通常超越国界,包括国际贸易开放。

p296.original:
A general orientation toward markets does not rule out important roles for government. There are times when markets fail to allocate capital or technology in a manner that provides the greatest benefit for society as a whole. The government's role is to correct these failures. In addition, government can guide or influence markets toward certain outcomes. The following examples highlight some important areas that governments around the world have chosen to invest in to facilitate capital deepening and technology:
  
        Education. The Danish government requires all children under 16 to attend school. They can choose to attend a public school (Folkeskole) or a private school. Students do not pay tuition to attend Folkeskole. Thirteen percent of primary/secondary (elementary/high) school is private, and the government supplies vouchers to citizens who choose private school.
Savings and Investment. In the United States, as in other countries, the government taxes gains from private investment. Low capital gains taxes encourage investment and so also economic growth.
Infrastructure. The Japanese government in the mid-1990s undertook significant infrastructure projects to improve roads and public works. This in turn increased the stock of physical capital and ultimately economic growth.
Special Economic Zones. The island of Mauritius is one of the few African nations to encourage international trade in government-supported special economic zones (SEZ). These are areas of the country, usually with access to a port where, among other benefits, the government does not tax trade. As a result of its SEZ, Mauritius has enjoyed above-average economic growth since the 1980s. Free trade does not have to occur in an SEZ however. Governments can encourage international trade across the board, or surrender to protectionism.
Scientific Research. The European Union has strong programs to invest in scientific research. The researchers Abraham García and Pierre Mohnen demonstrate that firms which received support from the Austrian government actually increased their research intensity and had more sales. Governments can support scientific research and technical training that helps to create and spread new technologies. Governments can also provide a legal environment that protects the ability of inventors to profit from their inventions.
p296.zh: 面向市场的总体方向并不排除政府的重要作用。 有时,市场未能以为整个社会提供最大利益的方式分配资本或技术。 政府的作用是纠正这些失误. 此外,政府可以引导或影响市场取得某些结果。 以下例子突出了世界各国政府为促进资本深化和技术而选择投资的一些重要领域:教育。 丹麦政府要求所有16岁以下的儿童上学。 他们可以选择上公立学校(Folkeskole)或私立学校.学生不缴纳学费参加Folkeskole。13%的小学/中学(小学/高中)是私立学校,政府向选择私立学校的公民提供券。储蓄和投资。在美国,与其他国家一样,政府税收从私人投资中收益.低资本收益税鼓励投资,也鼓励经济增长。基础设施。日本政府在1990年代中期开展了重大基础设施项目,以改善道路和公共工程。 这反过来又增加了有形资本的存量,并最终增加了经济增长。经济特区报.毛里求斯岛是鼓励政府支持的特别经济区国际贸易的少数非洲国家之一。这些地区是国家的地区,通常可以进入一个港口,除了其他好处外,政府不向该港口征税。毛里求斯由于其经济区,自1980年代以来实现了高于平均水平的经济增长。 但是,自由贸易不必在专属经济区内进行。 政府可以鼓励国际贸易全面发展,或者向保护主义投降。科学研究. 欧洲联盟在科学研究方面有强有力的投资方案。研究者亚伯拉罕·加西亚和皮埃尔·莫赫宁(Pierre Mohnen)证明,得到奥地利政府支持的公司实际上提高了研究强度,并拥有更多的销售额. 政府可以支持有助于创造和传播新技术的科学研究和技术培训。 政府也可以提供一种法律环境,保护发明者从其发明中获利的能力.

p297.original: There are many more ways in which the government can play an active role in promoting economic growth. We explore them in other chapters and in particular in Macroeconomic Policy Around the World. A healthy climate for growth in GDP per capita and labor productivity includes human capital deepening, physical capital deepening, and technological gains, operating in a market-oriented economy with supportive government policies.
p297.zh: 政府在促进经济增长方面可以发挥积极作用的还有许多其他方式。 我们在其他章节,特别是在《世界各地的宏观经济政策》中探讨这些问题。实现人均国内生产总值和劳动生产率增长的健康环境包括人力资本的深化、有形资本的深化和技术收益,在以市场为导向的经济中运作,政府采取支持性政策。

p299.original: Over decades and generations, seemingly small differences of a few percentage points in the annual rate of economic growth make an enormous difference in GDP per capita. Capital deepening refers to an increase in the amount of capital per worker, either human capital per worker, in the form of higher education or skills, or physical capital per worker. Technology, in its economic meaning, refers broadly to all new methods of production, which includes major scientific inventions but also small inventions and even better forms of management or other types of institutions. A healthy climate for growth in GDP per capita consists of improvements in human capital, physical capital, and technology, in a market-oriented environment with supportive public policies and institutions.
p299.zh: 几十年来和几代人之间,年经济增长率的几个百分点似乎差别不大,这在人均国内生产总值方面产生了巨大变化。资本深化,是指以高等教育或技能形式,或者以工人人均实际资本形式,增加工人人均资本金额.技术在经济意义上泛指所有新的生产方法,它包括主要的科学发明,但也包括小的发明,甚至更好的管理形式或其他类型的机构.人均国内生产总值增长的健康气候,包括在以市场为导向的环境中,利用支持性的公共政策和机构,人力资本、有形资本和技术的改善。

p301.original: What do the growth accounting studies conclude are the determinants of growth? Which is more important, the determinants or how they are combined?
p301.zh: 增长会计研究的结论是,增长的决定因素是什么?哪些是更重要的决定因素,或如何将它们结合起来?

p302.original: Capital deepening and technology are important. What seems to be more important is how they are combined.
p302.zh: 深化资本和技术建设具有重要意义.更重要的是,它们是如何结合在一起的。

p303.original: What policies can the government of a free-market economy implement to stimulate economic growth?
p303.zh: 自由市场经济政府可以实施哪些政策来刺激经济增长?

p304.original: Government can contribute to economic growth by investing in human capital through the education system, building a strong physical infrastructure for transportation and commerce, increasing investment by lowering capital gains taxes, creating special economic zones that allow for reduced tariffs, and investing in research and development.
p304.zh: 政府可以通过教育系统对人力资本进行投资,为运输和商业建设强大的有形基础设施,通过降低资本收益税增加投资,建立允许降低关税的特别经济区,以及对研发进行投资,从而促进经济增长。

p305.original: List the areas where government policy can help economic growth.
p305.zh: 列出政府政策能帮助经济增长的领域.

p392.original: Each of the countries in  has its own unique story of investments in human and physical capital, technological gains, market forces, government policies, and even lucky events, but an overall pattern of convergence is clear. The low-income countries have GDP growth that is faster than that of the middle-income countries, which in turn have GDP growth that is faster than that of the high-income countries. Two prominent members of the fast-growth club are China and India, which between them have nearly 40% of the world’s population. Some prominent members of the slow-growth club are high-income countries like France, Germany, Italy, and Japan.
p392.zh: 每个国家都有自己独特的经历,即投资于人力和物质资本、技术收益、市场力量、政府政策,甚至幸运事件,但总的趋同模式是明确的。低收入国家的国内生产总值增长快于中等收入国家,后者的国内生产总值增长快于高收入国家。 中国和印度是快速增长俱乐部的两大重要成员,它们之间拥有近40%的世界人口。慢增长俱乐部的一些突出成员是法国,德国,意大利,日本等高收入国家.

p393.original: Will this pattern of economic convergence persist into the future? This is a controversial question among economists that we will consider by looking at some of the main arguments on both sides.
p393.zh: 这种经济趋同的模式今后是否会继续存在? 这是一个经济学家之间有争议的问题,我们将通过研究双方的一些主要论点来考虑这个问题.

p395.original: Several arguments suggest that low-income countries might have an advantage in achieving greater worker productivity and economic growth in the future.
p395.zh: 一些论点表明,低收入国家在将来提高工人生产力和经济增长方面可能具有优势。

p396.original: A first argument is based on diminishing marginal returns. Even though deepening human and physical capital will tend to increase GDP per capita, the law of diminishing returns suggests that as an economy continues to increase its human and physical capital, the marginal gains to economic growth will diminish. For example, raising the average education level of the population by two years from a tenth-grade level to a high school diploma (while holding all other inputs constant) would produce a certain increase in output. An additional two-year increase, so that the average person had a two-year college degree, would increase output further, but the marginal gain would be smaller. Yet another additional two-year increase in the level of education, so that the average person would have a four-year-college bachelor’s degree, would increase output still further, but the marginal increase would again be smaller. A similar lesson holds for physical capital. If the quantity of physical capital available to the average worker increases, by, say, $5,000 to $10,000 (again, while holding all other inputs constant), it will increase the level of output. An additional increase from $10,000 to $15,000 will increase output further, but the marginal increase will be smaller.
p396.zh: 第一个论点是基于边际回报不断减少。 尽管深化的人力和物质资本往往会增加人均国内生产总值,但收益下降的法则表明,随着经济继续增加其人力和物质资本,经济增长的边际收益将减少。 例如,将人口平均教育水平从10年级提高到高中文凭(同时保持所有其他投入不变),将使产出有一定增长。额外增加两年时间,使一般人具有两年的大学学位,将进一步增加产出,但边际收益将较小。教育程度再增加两年,使普通人拥有四年的学士学位,将进一步增加产出,但边际增长将再次减少。同样的教训也包含在有形资本上。 如果平均工人可动用的实物资本数量增加,例如增加5 000美元至10 000美元(在保持所有其他投入不变的同时),则将增加产出水平。将产出从10 000美元增加到15 000美元,将进一步增加,但略有增加的幅度较小。

p397.original: Low-income countries like China and India tend to have lower levels of human capital and physical capital, so an investment in capital deepening should have a larger marginal effect in these countries than in high-income countries, where levels of human and physical capital are already relatively high. Diminishing returns implies that low-income economies could converge to the levels that the high-income countries achieve.
p397.zh: 中国和印度等低收入国家的人力资本和实物资本水平往往较低,因此,资本深化投资在这些国家应比高收入国家产生更大的边际影响,因为高收入国家的人力和实物资本水平已经较高。收益下降意味着低收入经济体可以趋同到高收入国家达到的水平。

p398.original: A second argument is that low-income countries may find it easier to improve their technologies than high-income countries. High-income countries must continually invent new technologies, whereas low-income countries can often find ways of applying technology that has already been invented and is well understood. The economist Alexander Gerschenkron (1904–1978) gave this phenomenon a memorable name: “the advantages of backwardness.” Of course, he did not literally mean that it is an advantage to have a lower standard of living. He was pointing out that a country that is behind has some extra potential for catching up.
p398.zh: 第二个论点是,低收入国家可能比高收入国家更容易改进技术。高收入国家必须不断发明新技术,而低收入国家往往能够找到应用已经发明并广为人知的技术的方法。经济学家亚历山大·格申克伦(1904年—1978年)给这一现象起了一个令人难忘的名字 : “ 落后的优势 ” 。 当然,他并没有从字面上说,低生活水平是一种优势。 他指出,一个落后的国家有某种额外的赶超潜力。

p399.original: Finally, optimists argue that many countries have observed the experience of those that have grown more quickly and have learned from it. Moreover, once the people of a country begin to enjoy the benefits of a higher standard of living, they may be more likely to build and support the market-friendly institutions that will help provide this standard of living.
p399.zh: 最后,乐观主义者认为,许多国家都观察到那些增长更快并从中吸取教训的国家的经验。 此外,一旦一国人民开始享受较高生活水平的好处,他们可能更可能建立和支持有助于提供这种生活水平的市场友好型机构。

p401.original: Arguments That Convergence Is neither Inevitable nor Likely

p402.original: If the economy's growth depended only on the deepening of human capital and physical capital, then we would expect that economy's growth rate to slow down over the long run because of diminishing marginal returns. However, there is another crucial factor in the aggregate production function: technology.
p402.zh: 如果经济的增长仅依赖于人力资本和有形资本的深化,那么我们预计经济的增长率会因边际回报下降而长期放缓. 然而,总生产功能中还有另一个关键因素:技术。

p403.original: Developing new technology can provide a way for an economy to sidestep the diminishing marginal returns of capital deepening.  shows how. The figure's horizontal axis measures the amount of capital deepening, which on this figure is an overall measure that includes deepening of both physical and human capital. The amount of human and physical capital per worker increases as you move from left to right, from C1 to C2 to C3. The diagram's vertical axis measures per capita output. Start by considering the lowest line in this diagram, labeled Technology 1. Along this aggregate production function, the level of technology is held constant, so the line shows only the relationship between capital deepening and output. As capital deepens from C1 to C2 to C3 and the economy moves from R to U to W, per capita output does increase—but the way in which the line starts out steeper on the left but then flattens as it moves to the right shows the diminishing marginal returns, as additional marginal amounts of capital deepening increase output by ever-smaller amounts. The shape of the aggregate production line (Technology 1) shows that the ability of capital deepening, by itself, to generate sustained economic growth is limited, since diminishing returns will eventually set in.
p403.zh: 开发新技术可以为经济提供一种途径,以避开资本不断加深的边际收益。数字的横向轴线衡量资本深化量,根据这一数字,这是包括深化有形资本和人力资本在内的总体计量。 随着从左向右,从C1到C2到C3的移动,每个工人的人力和实物资本金额增加. 图中的垂直轴测量人均产出. 首先考虑本图中的最低线条,标签为Technology 1.沿着这种总生产功能,技术水平保持不变,因此线条只显示资本深化与产出之间的关系. 随着资本从C1增长到C2增长到C3,随着经济从R增长到U增长,人均产出确实增加——但线路在左侧起步较陡,但在向右移动时逐渐平缓,这表明边际收益正在减少,因为资本增加的边际收益增加,其产出增加幅度越来越小。总体生产线的形状(技术1)表明,资本深化本身产生持续经济增长的能力是有限的,因为收益的下降最终会落到实处。

p405.original: Now, bring improvements in technology into the picture. Improved technology means that with a given set of inputs, more output is possible. The production function labeled Technology 1 in the figure is based on one level of technology, but Technology 2 is based on an improved level of technology, so for every level of capital deepening on the horizontal axis, it produces a higher level of output on the vertical axis. In turn, production function Technology 3 represents a still higher level of technology, so that for every level of inputs on the horizontal axis, it produces a higher level of output on the vertical axis than either of the other two aggregate production functions.
p405.zh: 现在,把技术的改进带入画面。改进技术意味着,有了一套特定的投入,就可以有更多的产出。 图中标注为技术1的生产功能以一级技术为基础,但技术2则以提高技术水平为基础,因此对于横向轴上每一级资本深化,在纵向轴上产生更高水平的输出.反过来,技术3代表了更高水平的技术,因此对于水平轴上的每一级投入,其垂直轴上的输出水平要高于其他两种总生产功能中的任何一种.

p406.original: Most healthy, growing economies are deepening their human and physical capital and increasing technology at the same time. As a result, the economy can move from a choice like point R on the Technology 1 aggregate production line to a point like S on Technology 2 and a point like T on the still higher aggregate production line (Technology 3). With the combination of technology and capital deepening, the rise in GDP per capita in high-income countries does not need to fade away because of diminishing returns. The gains from technology can offset the diminishing returns involved with capital deepening.
p406.zh: 最健康、增长的经济体正在深化其人力和物质资本,同时增加技术。 因此,经济可以从技术1号总生产线R点到技术2号S点,以及仍然较高的总生产线T点(技术3号)等选择. 随着技术和资本的不断深化,高收入国家人均国内生产总值的上升不必因收益的减少而消失。技术收益可以抵消资本深化带来的收益下降。

p407.original: Will technological improvements themselves run into diminishing returns over time? That is, will it become continually harder and more costly to discover new technological improvements? Perhaps someday, but, at least over the last two centuries since the beginning of the Industrial Revolution, improvements in technology have not run into diminishing marginal returns. Modern inventions, like the internet or discoveries in genetics or materials science, do not seem to provide smaller gains to output than earlier inventions like the steam engine or the railroad. One reason that technological ideas do not seem to run into diminishing returns is that we often can apply widely the ideas of new technology at a marginal cost that is very low or even zero. A specific worker or group of workers must use a specific additional machine, or an additional year of education. Many workers across the economy can use a new technology or invention at very low marginal cost.
p407.zh: 技术进步本身是否会随着时间推移而不断减少回报?也就是说,发现新的技术改进是否会变得更加困难和代价更高? 也许有一天,但至少自工业革命开始以来的最近两个世纪里,技术的改进并没有陷入微薄的回报.现代发明,如互联网或遗传学或材料科学的发现,似乎不会比蒸汽机或铁路等早期发明提供较小的输出收益.技术思想似乎没有达到下降回报的一个原因是,我们常常能够以很低甚至零的边际成本广泛应用新技术思想。特定劳动者或者劳动者群体必须使用特定的额外机器,或者额外教育年限.整个经济的许多工人可以以非常低的边际成本使用新技术或发明.

p408.original: The argument that it is easier for a low-income country to copy and adapt existing technology than it is for a high-income country to invent new technology is not necessarily true, either. When it comes to adapting and using new technology, a society’s performance is not necessarily guaranteed, but is the result of whether the country's economic, educational, and public policy institutions are supportive. In theory, perhaps, low-income countries have many opportunities to copy and adapt technology, but if they lack the appropriate supportive economic infrastructure and institutions, the theoretical possibility that backwardness might have certain advantages is of little practical relevance.
p408.zh: 关于低收入国家比高收入国家更容易复制和改造现有技术来发明新技术的论点也不一定是真的。 在改造和利用新技术方面,一个社会的表现不一定得到保障,而是国家的经济、教育和公共政策机构是否支持的结果。理论上说,也许低收入国家有许多机会复制和改造技术,但是,如果它们缺乏适当的支持性经济基础设施和机构,那么落后可能具有某些优势的理论可能性就没有什么实际意义。
