p411.original: Although economic convergence between the high-income countries and the rest of the world seems possible and even likely, it will proceed slowly. Consider, for example, a country that starts off with a GDP per capita of $40,000, which would roughly represent a typical high-income country today, and another country that starts out at $4,000, which is roughly the level in low-income but not impoverished countries like Indonesia, Guatemala, or Egypt. Say that the rich country chugs along at a 2% annual growth rate of GDP per capita, while the poorer country grows at the aggressive rate of 7% per year. After 30 years, GDP per capita in the rich country will be $72,450 (that is, $40,000 (1 + 0.02)30) while in the poor country it will be $30,450 (that is, $4,000 (1 + 0.07)30). Convergence has occurred. The rich country used to be 10 times as wealthy as the poor one, and now it is only about 2.4 times as wealthy. Even after 30 consecutive years of very rapid growth, however, people in the low-income country are still likely to feel quite poor compared to people in the rich country. Moreover, as the poor country catches up, its opportunities for catch-up growth are reduced, and its growth rate may slow down somewhat.
p411.zh: 尽管高收入国家与世界其他国家之间的经济趋同看来是可能的,甚至有可能,但经济趋同将缓慢进行。 例如,一个以人均国内生产总值40 000美元为起点的国家,大致相当于今天一个典型的高收入国家,另一个以4 000美元为起点的国家,这大致相当于印度尼西亚、危地马拉或埃及等低收入国家的贫困国家的水平。说富裕国家每年人均GDP增长率为2%,而较贫穷国家则以每年7%的猛烈增长。30年后,富国的人均GDP将达到72,450美元(即40,000美元(1+0.0230美元)),而穷国的人均GDP将达到30,450美元(即4,000美元(1+0.0730美元)。已而共现.富国曾经是穷国的十倍,现在只有富人大约2.4倍. 然而,即使在连续30年的非常快速增长之后,与富国人民相比,低收入国家人民仍然可能感到相当贫穷。 此外,随着穷国赶上,其赶超增长的机会减少,其增长率可能有所放缓。

p412.original: The slowness of convergence illustrates again that small differences in annual rates of economic growth become huge differences over time. The high-income countries have been building up their advantage in standard of living over decades—more than a century in some cases. Even in an optimistic scenario, it will take decades for the low-income countries of the world to catch up significantly.
p412.zh: 趋同速度缓慢再次表明,随着时间推移,年经济增长率的微小差异成为巨大的差异。高收入国家几十年来——在某些情况下超过一个世纪——在生活水平方面不断积累优势。即使在乐观的情况下,世界低收入国家也需要几十年的时间才能大大赶上。

p414.original: We can tell the story of modern economic growth by looking at calorie consumption over time. The dramatic rise in incomes allowed the average person to eat better and consume more calories. How did these incomes increase? The neoclassical growth consensus uses the aggregate production function to suggest that the period of modern economic growth came about because of increases in inputs such as technology and physical and human capital. Also important was the way in which technological progress combined with physical and human capital deepening to create growth and convergence. The issue of distribution of income notwithstanding, it is clear that the average worker can afford more calories in 2020 than in 1875.
p414.zh: 我们可以通过观察一段时间的卡路里消费来讲述现代经济增长的故事.收入的急剧增长使一般人能够更好地吃东西,消费更多的卡路里。 这些收入是如何增加的? 新古典主义的增长共识利用生产总量的功能来表明,现代经济增长时期的到来是由于技术和物质及人力资本等投入的增加。 同样重要的是,技术进步与有形和人力资本的深化相结合,以创造增长和趋同。 尽管存在收入分配问题,但很明显,平均工人在2020年能够承受的热量高于1875年。

p415.original: Aside from increases in income, there is another reason why the average person can afford more food. Modern agriculture has allowed many countries to produce more food than they need. Despite having more than enough food, however, many governments and multilateral agencies have not solved the food distribution problem. In fact, food shortages, famine, or general food insecurity are caused more often by the failure of government macroeconomic policy, according to the Nobel Prize-winning economist Amartya Sen. Sen has conducted extensive research into issues of inequality, poverty, and the role of government in improving standards of living. Macroeconomic policies that strive toward stable inflation, full employment, education of women, and preservation of property rights are more likely to eliminate starvation and provide for a more even distribution of food.
p415.zh: 除了增加收入之外,还有一个原因,即普通人能够负担更多的食物。现代农业使许多国家能够生产超出其需要的粮食。 然而,尽管粮食足够多,许多政府和多边机构仍未解决粮食分配问题。 事实上,根据诺贝尔奖得主经济学家阿马蒂亚·森(Amartya Sen)的说法,粮食短缺,饥荒,或普遍的粮食无保障,更多是政府宏观经济政策的失败造成的.森对不平等、贫穷和政府在提高生活水平方面的作用等问题进行了广泛的研究。力求稳定通货膨胀、充分就业、妇女教育和保护财产权的宏观经济政策,更有可能消除饥饿,实现粮食更均衡的分配。

p416.original: Because we have more food per capita, global food prices have decreased since 1875. The prices of some foods, however, have decreased more than the prices of others. For example, researchers from the University of Washington have shown that in the United States, calories from zucchini and lettuce are 100 times more expensive than calories from oil, butter, and sugar. Research from countries like India, China, and the United States suggests that as incomes rise, individuals want more calories from fats and protein and fewer from carbohydrates. This has very interesting implications for global food production, obesity, and environmental consequences. Affluent urban India has an obesity problem much like many parts of the United States. The forces of convergence are at work.
p416.zh: 因为我们人均粮食较多,全球粮食价格自1875年以来已经下降。 然而,一些食品的价格比其他食品的价格下跌得更多。 例如,华盛顿大学的研究人员已经表明,在美国,来自 ⁇ 基尼和生菜的热量比来自石油,黄油和糖的热量贵100倍. 印度、中国和美国等国的研究表明,随着收入的增加,个人希望从脂肪和蛋白质中获取更多的卡路里,而从碳水化合物中获取的卡路里则更少。 这对全球粮食生产、肥胖和环境后果有着非常有意义的影响。富裕的城市印度有肥胖症问题 与美国很多地区一样趋同的力量正在发挥作用。

p418.original: When countries with lower GDP levels per capita catch up to countries with higher GDP levels per capita, we call the process convergence. Convergence can occur even when both high- and low-income countries increase investment in physical and human capital with the objective of growing GDP. This is because the impact of new investment in physical and human capital on a low-income country may result in huge gains as new skills or equipment combine with the labor force. In higher-income countries, however, a level of investment equal to that of the low income country is not likely to have as big an impact, because the more developed country most likely already has high levels of capital investment. Therefore, the marginal gain from this additional investment tends to be successively less and less. Higher income countries are more likely to have diminishing returns to their investments and must continually invent new technologies. This allows lower-income economies to have a chance for convergent growth. However, many high-income economies have developed economic and political institutions that provide a healthy economic climate for an ongoing stream of technological innovations. Continuous technological innovation can counterbalance diminishing returns to investments in human and physical capital.
p418.zh: 当人均国内总产值水平较低的国家赶上人均国内总产值水平较高的国家时,我们称之为进程趋同。 即使高收入和低收入国家都增加了有形资本和人力资本的投资,以达到增加国内生产总值的目的,也可能出现趋同现象。这是因为,随着新的技能或设备与劳动力的结合,对有形资本和人力资本的新投资对低收入国家的影响可能带来巨大的收益。 然而,在较高收入国家,投资水平与低收入国家的投资水平不会产生如此大的影响,因为最可能的国家已经拥有高水平的资本投资。 因此,这种额外投资的边际收益往往相继越来越少。高收入国家的投资收益更有可能减少,必须不断发明新技术。这使低收入经济体有机会实现趋同增长。 然而,许多高收入经济体已建立了经济和政治机构,为不断进行的技术创新提供健康的经济环境。持续的技术创新能够抵消人力资本和实物资本投资收益的减少。

p420.original: Use an example to explain why, after periods of rapid growth, a low-income country that has not caught up to a high-income country may feel poor.
p420.zh: 举个例子,解释为什么一个没有赶上高收入国家的低收入国家在经历了快速增长之后可能感到贫穷。

p421.original: A good way to think about this is how a runner who has fallen behind in a race feels psychologically and physically as he catches up. Playing catch-up can be more taxing than maintaining one’s position at the head of the pack.
p421.zh: 一个很好的思考方式是,一个在比赛中落后的跑者在追上时,在心理上和身体上的感觉.赶超比保持个人在包头的地位更值得征税。

p422.original:
Would the following events usually lead to capital deepening? Why or why not?
        
A weak economy in which businesses become reluctant to make long-term investments in physical capital.
A rise in international trade.
A trend in which many more adults participate in continuing education courses through their employers and at colleges and universities.
p422.zh: 以下事件通常会导致资本的深化? 为什么或为什么不呢?经济疲软,企业不愿意对实物资本进行长期投资。国际贸易的兴起.这种趋势是,更多的成年人通过雇主和在大专院校参加继续教育课程。

p423.original:
No. Capital deepening refers to an increase in the amount of capital per person in an economy. A decrease in investment by firms will actually cause the opposite of capital deepening (since the population will grow over time).
There is no direct connection between an increase in international trade and capital deepening. One could imagine particular scenarios where trade could lead to capital deepening (for example, if international capital inflows—which are the counterpart to increasing the trade deficit—lead to an increase in physical capital investment), but in general, no.
Yes. Capital deepening refers to an increase in either physical capital or human capital per person. Continuing education or any time of lifelong learning adds to human capital and thus creates capital deepening.
p423.zh: 没有。资本深化是指经济中人均资本金额的增加.公司投资的减少实际上将导致资本的深化(因为随着时间的推移,人口将会增加)。国际贸易的增加与资本的深化之间没有直接联系。 人们可以想象贸易可能导致资本深化的具体情景(例如,如果国际资本流入——这是增加贸易赤字的对应因素——导致有形资本投资的增加),但一般而言,不是。 对资本深化,是指人人均有形资本或者人力资本的增加.继续教育或任何终生学习时间都会增加人力资本,从而加深资本。

p424.original: What are the “advantages of backwardness” for economic growth?
p424.zh: 经济增长的“落后优势”是什么?

p425.original: The advantages of backwardness include faster growth rates because of the process of convergence, as well as the ability to adopt new technologies that were developed first in the “leader” countries. While being “backward” is not inherently a good thing, Gerschenkron stressed that there are certain advantages which aid countries trying to “catch up.”
p425.zh: 落后的优点包括:由于趋同进程,增长率加快,以及有能力采用“领先”国家首先开发的新技术。格申克龙虽然“后退”本质上不是一件好事,但强调援助试图“追赶”的国家有某些好处。

p426.original: Would you expect capital deepening to result in diminished returns? Why or why not? Would you expect improvements in technology to result in diminished returns? Why or why not?
p426.zh: 你期望资本的深化会导致收益的减少吗? 为什么或为什么不呢? 您是否期望技术的改进会导致回报的减少? 为什么或为什么不呢?

p427.original: Capital deepening, by definition, should lead to diminished returns because you're investing more and more but using the same methods of production, leading to the marginal productivity declining. This is shown on a production function as a movement along the curve. Improvements in technology should not lead to diminished returns because you are finding new and more efficient ways of using the same amount of capital. This can be illustrated as a shift upward of the production function curve.
p427.zh: 资本的深化,顾名思义,应该会导致回报率的下降,因为你正在越来越多地投资,但使用相同的生产方法,导致边际生产力的下降.这一点在生产功能上显示为沿曲线运动.技术的改进不应导致收益的减少,因为你正在寻找新的、更有效的方法来使用同样数额的资本。 这可以说明生产功能曲线向上移动。

p428.original: Why does productivity growth in high-income economies not slow down as it runs into diminishing returns from additional investments in physical capital and human capital? Does this show one area where the theory of diminishing returns fails to apply? Why or why not?
p428.zh: 高收入经济体的生产力增长为何不放慢,因为其因对实物资本和人力资本进行额外投资而带来的收益正在减少? 这是否显示一个区域, 衰减返回的理论未能应用 ? 为什么或为什么不呢?

p429.original:
In high-income economies, diminishing returns to investments in physical and human capital may not apply because many high-income economies have developed economic and political institutions that provide a healthy economic climate for an ongoing stream of technological innovations. Continuous technological innovation can counterbalance diminishing returns to investments in human and physical capital. These two factors have the added effect of making additional technological advances even easier for these countries.
      As a result, productivity growth from new advances in technology will not increase at a diminishing rate or otherwise slow down because the new methods of production will be adopted relatively quickly and easily, at very low marginal cost.
p429.zh: 在高收入经济体中,有形资本和人力资本投资收益的减少可能不适用,因为许多高收入经济体已建立了经济和政治机构,为持续的技术创新提供健康的经济环境。持续的技术创新能够抵消人力资本和实物资本投资收益的减少。 这两个因素还产生了使这些国家取得更多技术进步更加容易的附加效应。 因此,新的技术进步所产生的生产力增长不会以下降的速度增长,也不会以其他方式放慢,因为新的生产方法将比较迅速和容易地采用,其边际成本非常低。

p431.original: For a high-income economy like the United States, what aggregate production function elements are most important in bringing about growth in GDP per capita? What about a middle-income country such as Brazil? A low-income country such as Niger?
p431.zh: 对于像美国这样的高收入经济体来说,什么生产总功能要素对于实现人均国内生产总值的增长最为重要? 巴西这样的中等收入国家呢?尼日尔这样的低收入国家?

p432.original: List some arguments for and against the likelihood of convergence.
p432.zh: 列出一些支持和反对趋同可能性的论点。

p434.original: What sorts of policies can governments implement to encourage convergence?
p434.zh: 政府可执行何种政策鼓励趋同?

p435.original: As technological change makes us more sedentary and food costs increase, obesity is likely. What factors do you think may limit obesity?
p435.zh: 由于技术变革使我们更加沉闷,食品成本增加,肥胖症就有可能发生。 你认为什么因素可以限制肥胖症?

c2.original: An aggregate production function shows what goes into producing the output for an overall economy. (a) This aggregate production function has GDP as its output. (b) This aggregate production function has GDP per capita as its output. Because we calculate it on a per-person basis, we already figure the labor input into the other factors and we do not need to list it separately.
c2.zh: 总体生产功能表明,生产总经济的产出将如何进行。(a) 这一总生产功能以国内生产总值为产出。(b) 这一总生产功能的人均国内生产总值为产出。因为我们按人计算,我们已经把劳动力投入算入其他因素,我们不需要单独列出。

c3.original: Output per hour worked is a measure of worker productivity. In the U.S. economy, worker productivity rose more quickly in the 1960s and the mid-1990s compared with the 1970s and 1980s. However, these growth-rate differences are only a few percentage points per year. Look carefully to see them in the changing slope of the line. The average U.S. worker produced over twice as much per hour in 2020 than they did in the 1970s. (Source: U.S. Department of Labor, Bureau of Labor Statistics.)
c3.zh: 每小时工作的产出是衡量工人生产率的一个尺度。在美国经济中,1960年代和1990年代中期,工人生产率的上升比1970年代和1980年代更快. 然而,这些增长率差异每年只有几个百分点。仔细看看,看他们在线条的斜坡变化中.2020年美国工人平均每小时产量比1970年代高出一倍以上.(资料来源:美国).劳工部,劳工统计局。 )

c4.original: U.S. growth in worker productivity was very high between 1947 and 1973. It then declined to lower levels in the later 1970s and the 1980s. The late 1990s and early 2000s saw productivity rebound, but then productivity sagged a bit between 2001 and 2020. Some think the productivity rebound of the late 1990s and early 2000s marks the start of a “new economy” built on higher productivity growth, but we cannot determine  this until more time has passed. (Source: U.S. Department of Labor, Bureau of Labor Statistics.)
c4.zh: 1947年至1973年间,美国工人生产力的增长率非常高. 随后在1970年代后期和1980年代下降到较低水平.1990年代后期和2000年代初,生产率出现回升,但随后生产率在2001年至2020年期间略有下降。一些人认为,1990年代末和2000年代初的生产力回升标志着建立在更高的生产力增长之上的“新经济”的开始,但是,在更多的时间过去之前,我们无法确定这一点。(资料来源:美国).劳工部,劳工统计局。 )

c5.original: Rising levels of education for persons 25 and older show the deepening of human capital in the U.S. economy. Even today, under one-third of U.S. adults have completed a four-year college degree. There is clearly room for additional deepening of human capital to occur. (Source: Penn World Tables, 10.0 https://www.rug.nl/ggdc/productivity/pwt/?lang=en)
c5.zh: 25岁及以上人口的教育水平不断提高,表明美国经济的人力资本不断深化.即使在今天,不到三分之一的美国成年人也完成了四年的大学学位.人力资本显然还有进一步深化的余地。(资料来源:宾州世界表,10.0 https://www.rug.nl/ggdc/productivity/pwt/?lang=en).

c6.original: The value of the physical capital, measured by plant and equipment, used by the average worker in the U.S. economy has risen over the decades. The increase may have leveled off a bit in the 1970s and 1980s, which were, not coincidentally, times of slower-than-usual growth in worker productivity. We see a renewed increase in physical capital per worker in the late 1990s, followed by a flattening in the early 2000s. (Source: Center for International Comparisons of Production, Income and Prices, University of Pennsylvania)
c6.zh: 以工厂和设备为衡量,美国经济中一般工人使用的有形资本价值在几十年中不断上升。 在1970年代和1980年代,增长可能有所减缓,这并非巧合,当时工人生产力的增长比平常慢。我们看到,1990年代末,每名工人的实物资本再次增加,2000年代初期又出现平息。(资料来源:宾夕法尼亚大学生产、收入和价格国际比较中心)

c8.original: Imagine that the economy starts at point R, with the level of physical and human capital C1 and the output per capita at G1. If the economy relies only on capital deepening, while remaining at the technology level shown by the Technology 1 line, then it would face diminishing marginal returns as it moved from point R to point U to point W. However, now imagine that capital deepening is combined with improvements in technology. Then, as capital deepens from C1 to C2, technology improves from Technology 1 to Technology 2, and the economy moves from R to S. Similarly, as capital deepens from C2 to C3, technology increases from Technology 2 to Technology 3, and the economy moves from S to T. With improvements in technology, there is no longer any reason that economic growth must necessarily slow down.
c8.zh: 想象经济从R点开始,实际和人力资本水平C1,人均产出为G1. 如果经济只依靠资本的深化,而保持技术1线所显示的技术水平,那么随着从R点到U点到W点的移动,它就会面临边际收益的不断减少. 然而,现在想象资本深化与技术改进相结合。 随后,随着资本从C1向C2的深化,技术从技术1向技术2的提升,经济也从R向S移动. 同样,随着资本从C2增长到C3,技术从Technology 2增长到Technology 3,经济从S向T发展. 随着技术的改进,经济增长必然会放慢,这已经没有任何理由了。
